title: Why is summer hotter if Earth is farther?

steps.title: Distance isn't the driver
steps.say: Yes, in northern summer Earth is actually farther from the Sun — so distance can't be what makes it hot.

ops.text:
Right! In northern summer Earth is
farther away — so distance is NOT the cause.

steps.title: Sunlight hits at an angle
steps.say: What matters is the angle of the sunlight. A tilted Earth makes the Sun's rays strike the northern half more directly.

ops.text: What matters: the ANGLE of sunlight.

steps.title: Direct vs slanted rays
steps.say: Direct rays pack energy into a small area. Slanted rays spread the same energy over a much wider area.

steps.title: Long days too
steps.say: The tilt also gives the summer half longer days, so the ground gets more hours of heating.

ops.text:
Bonus: the tilted half also gets longer days —
more hours of heating each day.

steps.title: Summary
steps.say: So seasons come from the tilt changing the angle of sunlight and the length of the day — not from distance.

ops.text: Seasons = tilt → sunlight angle + day length, not distance.
